cases.question: For the dispatch program, which path applies on September 12, September 13, and the one-day exception on September 15?
cases.answer: Path Amber applies September 12, Path Cobalt applies September 13, and Path Ivory applies only on September 15.

truth_claims.claim: Path Amber controls dispatch through September 12, including that day.
Path Cobalt controls dispatch beginning September 13.
Path Ivory replaces the ordinary dispatch path only on September 15.

turns.content: The signed dispatch baseline says: Path Amber controls dispatch through September 12, including that day.
Path Ivory is the standing route for the unrelated harbor cleanup program.
A training sheet demonstrates Path Cobalt on September 6 but explicitly has no operational effect.
The approved transition states: Path Cobalt controls dispatch beginning September 13. Publication does not shorten the Amber period.
Path Amber remains printed on archived dispatch forms for September 1 through September 12.
A vehicle inspection will temporarily close Path Cobalt on September 18, after the dates in question.
The signed one-day exception says: Path Ivory replaces the ordinary dispatch path only on September 15. Cobalt resumes after that date.
Path Ivory also serves a rehearsal on September 14, but that rehearsal is not a dispatch operation.
The September 15 exception report was filed on September 16 and confirms the exception ended that night.
A proposed October route would use Path Amber again, but it has not been approved.

cases.question: After all valid notices, which intake bay governs the October 3 shipment and which bay governs shipments from October 12 onward?
cases.answer: Bay Rowan governs the October 3 shipment, and Bay Cedar governs shipments from October 12 onward.

truth_claims.claim: The original October 3 intake record assigned the shipment to Bay Linden.
The signed correction retroactively replaces Bay Linden with Bay Rowan for the October 3 shipment.
Bay Cedar governs intake beginning October 12 and has no retroactive effect.

turns.content: The original October 3 intake record assigned the shipment to Bay Linden.
Bay Rowan received a different calibration crate on October 4.
A draft proposed Bay Cedar for all October shipments, but the draft was rejected.
Bay Linden remains available for parcel returns unrelated to intake shipments.
The signed correction retroactively replaces Bay Linden with Bay Rowan for the October 3 shipment. Filing on October 8 does not make Rowan prospective.
Bay Rowan hosts a safety inspection on October 9, separate from the corrected shipment record.
A training intake at Bay Cedar on October 10 does not activate the future policy.
The approved future notice states: Bay Cedar governs intake beginning October 12 and has no retroactive effect.
Bay Linden is being repainted after it ceased governing intake.
Bay Rowan continues to store the October 3 paperwork; storage location does not define current intake policy.

cases.question: Which inspection interval applies to Team Delta on November 9, to Team Echo on November 9, and to Team Delta on November 12?
cases.answer: Team Delta uses 14 hours on November 9, Team Echo uses 24 hours on November 9, and Team Delta uses 18 hours on November 12.

truth_claims.claim: The general inspection interval is 24 hours through November 10.
Team Delta alone uses a 14-hour interval on November 8 through November 10.

turns.content: The general inspection interval is 24 hours through November 10. It applies to all teams absent a scoped exception.
Team Echo tested an 18-hour interval on one device, but the test was not policy.
A draft would have given Team Delta a 12-hour interval for the entire month; it was rejected.
The approved scoped exception states: Team Delta alone uses a 14-hour interval on November 8 through November 10. Other teams keep the general interval.
Team Delta also uses a 14-hour battery charging cycle, which is separate from inspection.
Team Echo begins a three-day inventory count on November 8; inspection policy is unchanged.
The signed transition says: An 18-hour general interval begins November 11. The Delta exception ends before this general transition.
A 24-hour archive label remains on reports created under the old rule.
Team Delta completed an inspection under the new general interval on November 12.
Team Echo schedules an unrelated 14-hour maintenance window.

cases.question: After the corrected event record, which occurred first, the coral survey or the mooring repair, and by how many days?
cases.answer: The mooring repair occurred first, two days before the corrected coral survey date.

truth_claims.claim: The mooring repair occurred on December 7.
The signed correction establishes that the coral survey occurred on December 9, not December 5.

turns.content: The preliminary survey note listed the coral survey as December 5; that date was later found to be a transcription error.
The mooring repair occurred on December 7. Its report was filed the next day.
A buoy inspection occurred on December 4, but it was not the mooring repair.
A coral camera calibration occurred on December 6; it was not the survey.
The repair invoice was approved on December 11, which is not the repair date.
A draft chronology copied the preliminary December 5 survey date without checking the vessel log.
The signed correction establishes that the coral survey occurred on December 9, not December 5. The vessel log controls event time.
The coral samples entered storage on December 10, after the corrected survey date.
The repaired mooring was inspected on December 12; inspection is not repair.
An unrelated reef survey was scheduled for December 18.
